lessons.body:
**Today's session, to scale:**

```steps 10 Warm-up | 30 Learn | 40 Play | 10 Essentials
```

## Warm-up (10 minutes)

- Chromatic warm-up across all six strings, alternate picking
- Chord changes from last week, one minute

## Learn (30 minutes)

Final checks: running order, charts, equipment, tuning, outfits, timings, introductions. Run the whole programme once; rest your hands the day before.

## Understand it

Final preparation is about **removing every possible surprise**, so that on the day you only have to play.

**The checklist:**

- **Running order** — final, written, shared with everyone involved (band, sound, MC).
- **Charts** — printed or on a tablet, in order, with spares.
- **Equipment** — instrument serviced (strings settled, keyboard working), cables, tuner, capo, picks, stands, power, adaptors, batteries; spares of anything that can fail.
- **Tuning plan** — when and how you will tune between pieces.
- **Outfits** — decided, ready, comfortable to play in.
- **Timings** — arrival, sound check, start, your slot length.
- **Introductions** — written and practised aloud.
- **Logistics** — transport, who carries what, contact numbers.

**Run the whole programme once**, under performance conditions, a few days before. Then only touch-up practice: hard passages slowly, starts and endings.

**Rest your hands the day before** — light practice only. Muscles and tendons need recovery; tiredness causes mistakes. Sleep well; sleep also consolidates what you have practised.

**Mental preparation:** visualise the performance going well, from walking on to bowing. Plan your breathing routine for before you start.

## Key words

- **Running order:** the final sequence of the performance
- **Contingency:** a backup plan for something going wrong
- **Recovery:** rest that lets the body perform at its best

## Read and watch

- [Presentation skills](https://www.skillsyouneed.com/presentation-skills.html) — SkillsYouNeed

lessons.title: Graduation recital and portfolio
lessons.summary: The graduation performance and your three-year portfolio.
objectives: You will perform your graduation project
You will submit your portfolio
You will reflect on three years
lessons.body:
**Today's session, to scale:**

```steps 10 Warm-up | 30 Learn | 40 Play | 10 Essentials
```

## Warm-up (10 minutes)

- Chromatic warm-up across all six strings, alternate picking
- Chord changes from last week, one minute

## Learn (30 minutes)

Perform your project for families, mentors and the Club. Submit your **portfolio**: recordings from Years 1, 2 and 3, your compositions or arrangements, your mentoring reports and a reflection.

## Understand it

Graduation is the culmination of three years: performing your project for families, mentors and the Club, and submitting a portfolio that tells your musical story.

**The performance** — everything you have prepared: arrive early, sound-check, warm up, follow your routine, introduce your work, play with conviction, acknowledge the audience and everyone who supported you.

**The portfolio** should include:

- **Recordings from Years 1, 2 and 3** — the progression is the most powerful evidence there is.
- **Your compositions and arrangements** — scores, lead sheets or tab, with recordings.
- **Your graduation project** evidence — programme, recordings, charts, lesson plans or EP.
- **Mentoring reports** — the sessions you led and the progress of those you taught.
- **A reflection** (one to two pages):
  - Where you started and where you are now.
  - The moments that changed your playing.
  - What you learnt about practice, performance, leadership and yourself.
  - Your next goals — further study, a band, church music, teaching, production, music as a career or a lifelong passion.

**Organise it** — a folder with clear file names and an index document; backed up in two places.

**Thank the people** who made it possible — instructors, mentors, family, fellow musicians. Then keep playing: the habits you have built will carry you for life.

## Key words

- **Portfolio:** an organised record of your work and progress
- **Reflection:** a written review of learning and next steps
- **Graduation:** the completion of the programme

## Read and watch

- [File naming conventions](https://datamanagement.hms.harvard.edu/plan-design/file-naming-conventions) — Harvard Medical School Data Management
- [Back up your data](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/top-tips-for-staying-secure-online/always-back-up-your-most-important-data) — UK National Cyber Security Centre

## Play (40 minutes)

- Graduation recital
- Portfolio

## Practise at home (20 minutes a day)

1. Warm up with this week's scale
1. Work on: Graduation recital
1. Then: Portfolio
1. Record one take and listen back
1. **With an AI assistant —** Record yourself on your phone and listen back before anyone else hears it. AI can tell you about timing and tuning; it cannot tell you whether it moved anybody. That part is yours and your teacher's.

## Essentials (10 minutes)

**Graduation:** NGG is a beginning. Write your next step: an exam grade, a band, a church or school role, a course, or a release.

## Make it fit you

- **If this is new to you:** halve the tempo, practise hands (or strings) separately, and master one part before adding the next. Two clean minutes beat twenty messy ones.
- **If you already can:** Plan your first step after NGG with a date.

## This week's assignment

Submit your portfolio and a one-page reflection: who you were in Year 1, who you are now, and where you go next.

> Practise slowly first. Speed comes from playing it right, not from playing it fast.
